additional_checks.scope: A second agent independently viewed the diagram, practice and prompt PNGs, checked their content, lecturer/subtitle clearance, continuous prompt source, fictional labels and optional gallery renderer documentation. No core or media tests were rerun for documentation-only changes.

Expanded creator-facing instructions for continuous recording, explicit retake scope, complete-sentence re-recording, valid take selection, intentional teaching repetition, actual synchronized editing and cut review. README and SKILL links point to the detailed narration reference. An independent first-use review informed this change. No new speech-recognition capability, audio fixture or full-course media review is claimed; core scripts are unchanged.

additional_checks.check: Default final-file review and repair policy
additional_checks.scope: Clarified mandatory agent-led final-file review without a second user request, full subtitle text verification, actual-audio checks, edit and retake joins, chapter/playback boundaries, repair and re-export review, and blocking formal approval for unresolved major defects. Technical helper scope remains explicitly separate from speech semantics, OCR, viewing and listening. Independent review informed the distinction. This is a workflow documentation update; no new automatic speech/OCR inspection engine or newly reviewed course media is claimed.

limitations: This validation covers local synthetic fixtures and package structure, not a newly produced full-length course or commercial teaching outcome.
Only the listed macOS arm64 environment was executed. Linux, Windows and other versions are not validated platforms.
The bundled tools target 2560x1440 at 60 fps with 48000 Hz stereo. Other output standards require adapted tools and renewed validation.
ASR, speech comprehension, person segmentation and semantic editing depend on the agent environment; the package does not ship these models or external service credentials.
render_brand.py --project-style applies to diagram mode. Other artwork modes expose their documented series/speaker/font parameters.
mix_audio.py requires a BGM source. A no-BGM course uses the calibrated narration master directly.
